catalog_quote: [8.10, p.216] inherited length is never found on the ultima, and in most Bs dialects (except Mas, Sor, N-S, S-L, War) is restricted to the penult. All Bs speech varieties except some dialects of Kuy and Tsg retain phonemic accent. The following minimal pair is found in all dialects and establishes contrastive accent for PBS: punuq [pU:nuq] tree trunk < PBS *punuq and punuq [punuq] full < PBS *punuq. ... [8.10.2, p.218] In all Bs dialects studied, a closed penult is stressed. Thus, stress is predictable from the shape of the form ... Regardless of the accent on the base form, if morphophonemic changes produce a form with a CVC-penult, the penult is stressed. ... [3.1.3, pp.50-51] The accentual systems of all other Bs dialects have phonetic details involving both vowel length and stress. The vowel in an accented open penult (CV) is long: all dialects (but Kuy and Tsg) bataq → ba:taq young…

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: every segment of the deciding quotation is present in the Zorc 1977 PDF we hold at the stated pdf pages 240, 242 and 74-75 (letter-spaced scanned, accents lost, substance verbatim); Bty = Bantayan I. confirmed in Zorc's sigla. (2) Deciding source is a 1977 comparative dialect survey whose accent statements are explicitly pan-Bisayan ('all Bs dialects studied', exceptions named and Bty not among them); Glottolog lists nothing else descriptive for bant1293. (3) Search located and downloaded the one Bantayanon-specific description, Allen 2022 (Tulane PhD, open, 198 pp): p.90 'stress is contrastive' with minimal pair ánay 'termite' / anáy 'sow', p.143 hábuy 'blanket' / habúy 'dull', and pp.90-91 non-neutral suffixes -an/-un move stress rightward to the new penult — this independently confirms lexical (contrastive penult/ultima accent with morphological conditioning) for this exact lan

sources.note: Only Bantayanon-specific grammatical description in existence; our record rested solely on Zorc's pan-Bisayan 1977 survey statements. downloaded now: confirms contrastive stress with Bty minimal pairs (ánay/anáy, hábuy/habúy) and suffix-induced rightward stress shift; should be added as a second citation.

sources.quote: No Bantayanon stress rule stated; Bantayanon forms are cited with lexical accent marks (Table 4.14: 'ka nákon', 'kamó nákon'); general remark p.287 fn.3 that some Philippine subgroup members have lost contrastive stress while others retain it (Bikol, Cordilleran; most Mindanao languages lost it) — Bantayanon not named among losers.

tone.quote: Stress involves the raising of one syllable’s prominence relative to other syllables via increased pitch, loudness, and length and a change in vowel quality (Aikhenvald, 2015, p. 47). Linawis has phonemic stress (see Table 8) but not phonemic length. Vowel length in the variety is caused by one of two phenomena. One, stress placement in the open penultimate syllable causes vowels to be realized as lengthened, but this does not occur in stressed closed penultimate and ultimate syllables. [...] [Abstract, p.1:] The variety has 15 consonant phonemes, three vowel phonemes, phonemic stress, and four major morphosyntactic classes

tone.quote: The researcher also observed that although Bantayanon and Sebuano have the highest number of similar lexical items, Bantayanon sounded more like Hiligaynon and its intonation is closest to Samar-Leyte’s. These findings support the contention that the five languages under study belong to the same group of languages.
